- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), cap forecast at +5% above prior peak to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–3 days (especially in early forecast window), adjust downward by 1–3% per lag day.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤ 0.10), model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show strong downward trend, model tends to overcorrect upward; apply downward bias of 2–4% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.50 spikes, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment peaks by 1–2% per sentiment unit.
